card.name: Just before a foreign-language term
card.fires_on: Punctuation or a joining word right before a transliterated non-English term, such as an opening bracket before a Chinese pinyin name or a comma before a Hebrew word. It is seen in discussions of Chinese medicine, Hebrew words and other foreign terms.

modes.label: Bracket before pinyin or Chinese
modes.description: An opening parenthesis after an English term, followed by its Chinese name or pinyin.

modes.label: Comma or link before Hebrew term
modes.description: A comma, "are" or "while" right before a Hebrew word or its gloss.
modes.example: Hebrew emunah means "belief" or "faith,"<< while>> emet means "truth."

card.writes: It promotes short romanized syllables such as jian, jin and hak, so it adds the start of a transliterated foreign word.
card.plain: It fires at the spot where a foreign-language name, often Chinese or Hebrew, is about to be given in Latin letters.
